title: "Trans ID In Free Fall": After Decade-Long Surge, Far Fewer Teens Identify As Lesbian, Gay, Or Bisexual
desc:
"Trans ID In Free Fall": After Decade-Long Surge, Far Fewer Teens Identify As Lesbian, Gay, Or Bisexual

Authored by Janice Hisle via The Epoch Times,

The percentage of American high schoolers who say they are homosexual or bisexual has plummeted after years on the rise.

Based on data from the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, psychologist and researcher Jean Twenge found that "the decline appears to be driven almost entirely by girls."

Girls identifying as lesbian, gay, or bisexual dropped 5 percentage points, hitting 22 percent last year. Among boys, that percentage fell by 2 percentage points to 7 percent.

"The trends are striking," especially compared to data from a decade ago, Twenge, a professor at San Diego State University, wrote on her blog in late September.

Reasons for the decline in teen in lesbian, gay, or bisexual identification are not readily apparent. "I have to confess: I have no idea," Twenge wrote.

Determining whether the numbers reflect the start of a trend requires further examination, she and other professionals say.

Competing explanations for the shift are emerging amid a larger debate over alternative sexuality in America.

Patterns Emerge

By comparing the CDC's newly released 2025 Youth Risk Behavior Survey with its 2023 figures for grades 9 through 12, Twenge identified a pattern: The younger the grade level, the sharper the decline in lesbian, gay, or bisexual identification.

Ninth graders calling themselves lesbian, gay, or bisexual dropped from 17 to 11 percent.

For 12th-grade students, the number dipped by 2 points, from 18 to 16 percent.

Twenge's analysis excluded responses from students who said they describe their sexual orientation "another way," were unsure, or didn't understand the survey question.

Identifying as transgender - which is a gender identity, rather than a sexual orientation - also was not specifically addressed.

The newly reported drops contrast with data from preceding years.

With 2015 as a baseline, the number of girls identifying as lesbian, gay, or bisexual ballooned 128 percent in six years; for boys, the number went up 99 percent in eight years, Twenge wrote.

At the same time, the percentage of young adults aged 18 to 24 identifying as lesbian, gay, or bisexual "is no longer racing upward as it did between 2014 and 2022," Twenge wrote in another blog post.

In 'Free Fall'?

A few studies appear to reflect findings similar to those Twenge described in the CDC data.

Between 2022 and 2025, students identifying as "straight" or heterosexual climbed from 76 percent to 83 percent, the University of Minnesota reported. That study surveyed Minnesota schoolchildren in grades 5, 8, 9, and 11.

And, a year ago, Canadian political science professor Eric Kaufmann pointed to a few studies reporting non-heterosexuality was dropping among high schoolers and college students.

The data showed "trans identification is in free fall among the young," he wrote on X.

Twenge referenced Kaufmann's quote and wrote that while declining lesbian, gay, or bisexual identification is not dramatic in older teens, the data for ninth graders "really does look like a free fall."

That observation about Generation Alpha - young people born in 2010 or later - "could be a harbinger of a coming wave of change, or it could be a blip - it's hard to say," Twenge wrote.

Presidential Politics

Liberals and conservatives alike opined that the pro-traditional-family policies of President Donald Trump appear to be playing a role.

Terry Schilling, president of the American Principles Project, which combats "anti-family extremism," told The Epoch Times that his organization has supported the Trump administration's efforts to "eliminate transgender ideology from school curriculum" and to ban boys from playing in girls' sports.

The administration has done a good job overall with "getting this type of ideology out of our schools, and instead embracing normalcy," he said.

A married father of eight, Schilling said: "It's very clear across all social data that families are incredibly important to someone's fulfillment and happiness and well-being in life."

He has witnessed lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transsexual ideology tearing families apart and distorting what "love" means.

"So many of these young people are getting lost in this seemingly attractive ideology that proposes tolerance and acceptance - when, ultimately, it doesn't provide either of those things," Schilling said. "It's eliminating anyone in their lives that might have concerns or questions about these newfound identities, it's just a totally tragic and sad political ideology that's taking hold."

'Oppression'

Biology professor and blogger PZ Myers, who calls himself a "godless liberal," is skeptical about the CDC data possibly revealing a trend.

"Are teenagers actually becoming straight again? That makes no sense," he wrote in an essay.

Those young people are "in the process of discovering their sexuality; it's not as if ten year olds were biased towards gayness and then 'straightened up' when they were 15," Myers wrote on his blog.

His essay - titled, "Oppression Works!" - implies that the respondents may have been unwilling to admit they are lesbian, gay, or bisexual in the current political climate.

"This is not a good time to honestly express yourself, because the [expletive] crazy Republicans are running roughshod over schools, education, and science," Myers wrote.

The data Twenge compiled shows that a slight drop in lesbian, gay, or bisexual identification began in 2021 for students in ninth and tenth grades. That year, Trump ended his first term in office.

More noticeable declines began around 2024, during Democratic President Joe Biden's tenure, even though his administration advanced pro-LGBT policies.

'Fad' Versus Human Nature

Politics aside, Pennsylvania licensed professional counselor Andrew Rodriguez believes cultural influences and human nature could be driving the decrease, if it holds.

"It's clear there was a social contagion, because of the 'fad' aspect of this," he told The Epoch Times. "And now people are starting to realize, 'Oh, this isn't truly who I am.'"

"Social engineering" - using society-wide influences to steer a culture in a desired direction - helped make identifying as lesbian, gay, or bisexual socially acceptable or even cool, especially for girls, Rodriguez said.

For some young people, "it just was an idea, and they jumped on it ... there was some social capital they got out of it, and now they're realizing that's not as popular anymore," he said.

Rodriguez, who owns and operates Integrity Christian Counseling, said he believes God instilled people with a drive toward unions with the opposite sex.

He thinks more girls are probably realizing "I really do want to be a wife and mom."

Texas psychologist David Pickup said a recent historic U.S. Supreme Court ruling will help more people face "reality" about sexuality and gender.

In Chiles v. Salazar, the court held that a Colorado law violated therapist Kaley Chiles's constitutional right to fully explore sex and gender issues with some clients.

Pickup leads a group that includes therapists, scholars, and researchers who believe adolescents and their parents "should not be pressured to affirm homosexual identity."

With the ruling, coupled with other societal shifts, "some people are realizing that LGBT issues are not inborn and change is possible," Pickup said.

LucccA asks: Why are labor unions in the US still not as well-organized compared to the rest of the world? I know there was a push against them in the past—does that still have an effect today? Also, why are there so many right-leaning unions in the US?

Michael: A lot of reasons. The US has low union density compared to other wealthy nations, currently at 10.0%, and that has been on a precipitous decline for the past few decades for a variety of reasons that include anti-union and union busting campaigns, outdated labor laws where employers often retaliate for union organizing or delay bargaining for years, as we are seeing with Starbucks, where there is no union contract after nearly five years since the first store won its union election in December 2021.Right to work laws in the US also undermine labor unions and starve them of resources. To the extent that there are right leaning labor unions in the US, they typically are law enforcement unions that consistently endorse and back Republican candidates despite the Republican Party in the US opposing collective bargaining. Some unions like the Teamsters have been making efforts to get Republicans to support legislation and in turn receive endorsements from the union, and this has shown up this election cycle with the Teamsters endorsing Republicans like Congressman Max Miller or Kansas Senator Roger Marshall, who are both facing very competitive re-election battles.

Heather: There’s a bunch of ideas floating around on cutting costs for groceries, healthcare and energy bills. A key thing Democrats are promising if they regain power in Congress is to wrestle back authority on trade and repeal Trump’s tariffs, which would lower what it costs compaines to import. A second is to advance a vote to stop the war in Iran, which could calm fuel prices. If Democrats retake the Senate, expect Elizabeth Warren to become chair of the powerful banking committe, and push forward some curbs on private equity investments. And Democrats have been coalescing around more government funding for childcare, a notable move to the left in recent years. Hakeem Jeffries, who will be House Speaker if Democrats win there, is promising to reinstate ACA tax cuts and roll back Medicaid cuts, but the party is divided on Medicare For All, with DSA candidates making promises on the campaign trail and more centrist Dems being pretty quiet.

Republicans running for Congress have been talking a lot about ways to lower gas prices, especially suspending the fuel tax, and shaving utility bills by making tech companies and other big users pay more. One Of The Longest-Running Partnerships In Fast-Food Industry Comes To A Sudden End
desc:
One Of The Longest-Running Partnerships In Fast-Food Industry Comes To A Sudden End

KFC plans to ditch Pepsi in favor of Coca-Cola at thousands of restaurants across the United States, ending one of the longest-running partnerships in fast-food history.

The fried chicken giant confirmed Thursday that it will begin replacing Pepsi products with Coca-Cola beverages in January 2027, with the transition expected to reach all of its roughly 3,700 American locations by spring.

The seemingly sudden move brings an end to a relationship dating back to 1986, when PepsiCo acquired KFC as part of its expansion into the restaurant business.

Despite PepsiCo spinning off KFC in 1997, the beverage giant continued supplying drinks to the chain for nearly three decades under its parent company, Yum! Brands.

Catherine Tan-Gillespie, KFC's president of U.S. operations, called the decision a major step in the company's broader effort to revitalize its restaurants and attract customers amid pressure from activist investor Elliott Investment Management.

"This partnership is about more than what's in the cup," Tan-Gillespie said in a statement. "It is another step in our work to evolve KFC, strengthen our restaurants, menu offerings and create a more relevant experience for today's customers."

The shake-up represents a significant victory for Coca-Cola in its decades-long rivalry with PepsiCo, particularly as the latter struggles with sluggish beverage sales and mounting pressure to improve its North American business.

Coca-Cola executive Dagmar Boggs hailed the new partnership as a major milestone for the beverage giant.

"By pairing KFC's iconic food and flavors with the breadth of Coca-Cola's beverage portfolio and innovation capabilities, we have an incredible opportunity to make every visit more refreshing, create memorable consumer experiences and unlock new growth possibilities together," Boggs told Fox Business.

title: Groups Sue DHS, Alleging Effort To Compile Voter Data Is Illegal
desc:
Groups Sue DHS, Alleging Effort To Compile Voter Data Is Illegal

Authored by Zachary Stieber via The Epoch Times,

Federal officials obtaining and compiling data on voters as part of an effort to combat voter fraud is illegal, three organizations said in an Oct. 15 lawsuit.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) compilation of the data from nearly every state violates the Privacy Act, which only lets agencies maintain information that is relevant and necessary for authorized purposes, the League of Women Voters, the Electronic Privacy Information Center, and the League of United Latin American Citizens said in the lawsuit, filed in federal court in the District of Columbia.

"Congress created DHS to prevent terrorism, secure the border, and address other specified threats - not to conduct a voter-fraud dragnet centered on the private voting information of millions of Americans and records reflecting the exercise of constitutional rights essential to democracy," the plaintiffs said.

DHS did not respond to a request for comment by the time of publication.

Federal law requires states to keep lists of registered voters. The lists always have the names of all registered voters, and usually include other details such as their addresses, sex, date of birth, and partial or complete Social Security number.

Certain individuals can request the data from states, but there are restrictions on requesters and other restrictions on disclosure.

For instance, most states do not allow people who obtain the data to disclose Social Security numbers.

The Privacy Act states in part that for information concerning activity protected by the U.S. Constitution's First Amendment, agencies can "maintain no record describing how any individual exercises rights guaranteed by the First Amendment unless expressly authorized by statute or by the individual about whom the record is maintained or unless pertinent to and within the scope of an authorized law enforcement activity."

The Department of Justice has been sharing voter lists it obtained with DHS, according to letters released by the government. DHS has obtained some version of voter registration lists from at least 47 states, according to the lawsuit.

The Department of Justice's Office of Legal Counsel said in a May legal opinion that the department "has authority to seek statewide voter lists and share them with the Department of Homeland Security as part of its effort to identify individuals who are ineligible to vote."

The office also said that DHS is "authorized by law to investigate ... voter fraud."

DHS has since been reviewing the data, along with information it purchased from commercial sources, to try to identify people who are not eligible to vote. In litigation filed separately on Thursday, the government said an analysis of the list and federal data showed that more than 20,000 people registered to vote in California are likely noncitizens.

The lawsuit shows that DHS possesses voter files for California and is improperly using them for election administration purposes, the League of Women Voters and the other plaintiffs said in the District of Columbia filing.

They're asking the court to declare the voter data collection policy violates federal law, enjoin government officials from carrying out the policy, and to order officials to delete information it has collected.

"The federal government has no business secretly collecting the sensitive personal information of millions of American voters and feeding it into immigration enforcement systems under the guise of election security," Celina Stewart, the CEO of the League of Women Voters, said in a statement.

"Let's be clear: Voting is a fundamental right, not a privilege granted by this administration, and our personal information is not theirs to exploit. The League will not stand by while this administration weaponizes voter data, undermines public trust, and threatens our fundamental freedoms."

title: Russia Celebrates 'Historic Moment' After Trump Formally Waives Graham Act Sanctions
desc:
Russia Celebrates 'Historic Moment' After Trump Formally Waives Graham Act Sanctions

The Kremlin is praising the Trump White House after the US President on Friday signed an executive order to waive a new package of sanctions and tariffs on Russia.

What's essentially a major and unexpected 'stay of execution' comes after in September Trump had signed the "Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026" into law.

It was expected to take effect soon, as part of a big Washington ramping up of pressure to further strangle the Russian economy and thus starve Putin's war machine.

Trump has informed Congress that he must waive the new sanctions package because it is in the US national interest, at a moment he's desperately trying to get diesel prices under control amid both the Iran war and Ukraine's attacks on Russian oil refineries.

"I have submitted to the Congress a certification that the issuance of such a waiver at this time is in the national interests of the United States," the president said in his order.

The significant reversal comes weeks before US midterm elections, and appears a serious extension and overture related to the earlier diesel deal struck between Putin and Trump.

Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev has hailed the move to put sanctions on hold as a "significant and truly historic moment."

He further said that enacting the package likely would have "brought economic cooperation between Russia and the US to a complete standstill."

Had Trump finally pulled the trigger on the measure, it would have slapped tariffs of up to 100% within 30 days on imports from Russia's top five oil and gas buyers, as well as any nation that knowingly purchased Russian fuel or actively helped Moscow evade sanctions

Needless to say, the Zelensky government sees this as yet more huge 'betrayal' by Trump and Washington, despite the billions in US and European taxpayer dollars already sunk into Kiev's coffers.

In a Saturday morning social media post, Zelensky accused Trump of essentially once again siding with Moscow, while also lamenting the loss of his friend Lindsey, and now also the loss of the sweeping sanctions package named after the late South Caroline Senator...

Sanctions relief will continue. I think the diesel deal and the move regarding the Lindsey Graham Act are not the end of it. Unfortunately. It’s unfortunate because we all had great respect for Lindsey. He devoted his life to America. We had an excellent relationship with him. And shortly before the tragedy, Lindsey was in Ukraine. He always supported us very strongly and pushed for as much assistance to Ukraine as possible. It’s difficult without him, I’ll be honest. I want to thank both Democrats and Republicans who supported his bill. That was a major victory: this truly bipartisan support. And now, the decision to undo all of this, to block all of it, seems wrong to me. And it definitely helps only the Russians. It only fuels their satisfaction and their desire to keep killing people. This certainly does not stop the war. From answers to journalists’ questions. (1/3)

— Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський (@ZelenskyyUa) October 17, 2026

title: Gen Z Life Satisfaction Plummets, 1 In 4 Receiving Treatment For Depression; New Poll Finds
desc:
Gen Z Life Satisfaction Plummets, 1 In 4 Receiving Treatment For Depression; New Poll Finds

Authored by Bryan Hyde via American Greatness,

A recent Gallup Life Evaluation Index poll shows that Generation Z's mental health and life satisfaction have plummeted, completely inverting historical happiness trends.

The New York Post reports that less than half now describe their lives as "thriving," compared to their Millennial predecessors a generation ago.

According to Gallup, more than a quarter of adults aged 18 to 29 also reported that they are being treated for depression, up by 11 points since 2019.

Thriving among U.S. adults aged 18 to 29 fell from 64% in 2010 to 44% through the third quarter of 2026 - a 20-point drop and the largest decline of any age group since tracking began.

New research from Gallup and @RippelHealth: https://t.co/TtC6Q7KTfI pic.twitter.com/Su1nfSJbXq

— Gallup (@Gallup) October 5, 2026

Historically, happiness data followed a predictable "U-shape" curve, where well-being peaked in youth, dipped during midlife, and rose again in retirement.

Today, global and domestic polling reveals that the curve has effectively flattened or reversed into a downward ski slope, with young adults reporting the highest rates of despair, anxiety, and misery.

Dr. Katrina Furey, MD, a Connecticut-based psychiatrist told the NY Post, "Gen Z has had constant access to their smart phones and social media, plus a global pandemic plus financial stressors like housing that no other generation has had."

Furey added, "The social isolation of COVID-19 during their formative developmental years for sure has left a lasting impact. Depression and loneliness can really tie into your social connections. And I do hear a lot of distress from that generation about their future."

The Gallup survey showed only 44 percent of young adults described themselves as "thriving," compared to 64 percent of the same age group back in 2010.

While Gen Z were the least positive generation, Millennials also showed a noticeable decline, with just 45 percent of those aged between 30-44 "thriving."

Meanwhile, Gen X positivity hasn't dropped as much as younger groups, but the 46% of those aged 45 to 64 now thriving matches their generation's low from 2008 during the height of the Great Recession, according to Gallup.

Researchers say the only generation that has higher life evaluations now than in 2008 is Baby Boomers, with the percentage of those aged 65 and older who are "thriving" rising steadily from 38% in 2008 to 53% in 2026, matching their record high of 2021.

Sociologists, economists, and psychologists attribute the multi-faceted crisis to a "perfect storm" of technological, financial, and societal shifts.

title: Evacuation Orders Issued As Wildfire Burns Homes In Southern California
desc:
Evacuation Orders Issued As Wildfire Burns Homes In Southern California

Authored by Jill McLaughlin via The Epoch Times,

Evacuation orders have been issued after a wind-fueled wildfire ignited Friday in a Southern California coastal community, burning through homes and 465 acres, fire authorities said.

The fire started in vegetation in San Clemente, and strong winds quickly pushed it into neighboring San Juan Capistrano in Orange County.

Fire authorities received a report at 11:33 a.m. Friday. The blaze grew to cover an area equal to about 350 football fields by 5 p.m., according to fire authorities.

"We rapidly launched an assault of air and ground resources to head towards this fire," Orange County Fire Authority Division Fire Chief Mark Backoff said in an update on social media. "We can confirm six homes have either been damaged or destroyed by this fire. Our hearts go out to the folks that are impacted by that."

Videos taken by local news outlets at the scene showed flames reaching a neighborhood off Via La Mirada in San Juan Capistrano at the north end of the blaze. Homes were quickly engulfed as firefighters attacked the flames to stop them from jumping to the next house.

One firefighter was overcome with heat exhaustion fighting the fire, Backoff said.

The department had prepared for the wind event, placing equipment in the area before the fire started, Backoff said.

Winds Whip Up Flames

Santa Ana Winds, a regional weather phenomenon that produces strong winds and dry, warm conditions, helped the blaze expand rapidly and pushed flames into residential neighborhoods.

Holy crap. San Clemente, California looks like HELL right now during this raging Norte Fire that sparked today Pray for the winds to calm down. And if you’re under an evacuation order, leave! https://t.co/8Wp5sqwKjd

— Nick Sortor (@nicksortor) October 16, 2026

Wind gusts reached 69 miles per hour in Orange County's Santiago Canyon and were measured at 45 miles per hour at the John Wayne Airport, according to the National Weather Service.

The Santa Ana Winds also fueled last year's deadly and destructive Palisades and Eaton fires in Los Angeles County.

Orange County and San Diego County coastal areas were under a heat advisory Friday as temperatures were expected to reach the mid-90s in some cities.

Meanwhile, on Wednesday and Thursday, Gov. Gavin Newsom directed Cal Fire and OES to pre-position resources and activated the State Operations Center ahead of the expected Santa Ana winds and heightened fire danger. Newsom also declared a state of emergency in four counties, including Los Angeles and Orange, on Thursday to support recovery from Tropical Storm Rachel.

"California is confronting these threats head-on," Newsom said.

Newsom directed the state's emergency services and the California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (Cal Fire) to move firefighters, engines, aircraft, and special equipment into the region.

🚨 BREAKING: WILDFIRES SPREAD ACROSS SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA AS THOUSANDS FACE EVACUATIONS

Multiple wildfires are burning across Southern California as powerful Santa Ana winds, dry vegetation, and unusually hot temperatures fuel dangerous fire conditions. One of the most… pic.twitter.com/rfKE0d22la

— Mighty News (@Mighty__News) October 17, 2026

Cal Fire is investigating the cause of the fire.

Evacuation orders were issued for several neighborhoods in San Juan Capistrano. The city opened shelters at its community center.

Fire authorities said more than 500 firefighters were assigned to the fire, and more resources were en route.

Thousands of people statewide had their power shut off before the winds picked up. About 134,000 customers were without electricity after Southern California Edison implemented a public safety power shutoff ahead of Friday's wind event.

Another wildfire started Thursday in the coastal city of Malibu. The city was still recovering from damage sustained in the Palisades Fire last year.

Malibu firefighters contained nearly 40 percent of the wildfire by Friday afternoon, and it had grown to 147 acres, fire authorities reported.

title: "Replacing Europe": Undercover Film Follows The Money Behind Europe's Taxpayer-Funded Mass Migration Pipeline
desc:
"Replacing Europe": Undercover Film Follows The Money Behind Europe's Taxpayer-Funded Mass Migration Pipeline

A new documentary from investigative outlet Muckraker traces the migrant route from West Africa through Spain and France to Britain, examining what the outlet describes as a network sustained by taxpayer-funded aid programs, NGOs, and even Western governments.

The 47-minute film, "Replacing Europe," draws on months of reporting and undercover footage to investigate the logistics and top NGO players behind the nation-killing mass migration into Europe.

"The entire migration is a game," says Sheikh M. Kromah, identified by Muckraker as a worker for the UN's International Organization for Migration. He alleges that Spain has a financial incentive to maintain arrivals because reducing them could jeopardize EU funding.

Muckraker claims that publicly funded institutions help sustain the migration flows that European governments publicly promise to control. Its interviews raise questions about oversight, spending incentives and the boundary between humanitarian assistance and facilitating illegal alien border crossings into Europe.

The broader concern is whether mass migration, malassimilation, and soaring public costs of the European welfare state that cater to migrants could compound fiscal pressure and political instability.

Here is Muckraker's report:

A UN migration worker admits Spain won't stop the boats because the EU money is too good. A Catholic NGO pulling in €225 million a year moves arrivals to the mainland and pays them to stay. Activists paint a trail to the French border. And the journalists who filmed it were attacked and nearly arrested.

Investigative outlet Muckraker spent two months following the West African migration route from start to finish: from the smuggling hub of Nouadhibou, Mauritania, to Spain's Canary Islands, across mainland Spain and France, and finally to the English Channel and the United Kingdom. The result is a new documentary, REPLACING EUROPE.

The film's central finding is that the movement of tens of thousands of illegal immigrants into Europe is not chaos. It is a managed system, run by smugglers, publicly funded NGOs, activist networks and governments, several of which admit on camera that they profit from it.

Among the documentary's findings:

  • A worker for the UN's International Organization for Migration says Spain deliberately lets the boats keep coming so it keeps receiving EU money.
  • ACCEM, a Catholic NGO that took in about €225 million in 2024, mostly from the Spanish state, moves arrivals from the Canary Islands to the mainland, houses them in camps and pays them a monthly allowance.
  • Migrants are flown by the hundreds from Gran Canaria to Madrid.
  • In the Spanish border town of Irun, an activist group has painted a trail of footsteps guiding migrants past police and into France, where a city-run shelter takes in people with no papers.
  • The UN's own migration agency says the priority should be "facilitating, not restricting" migration.

Where It Starts: Mauritania

Most boats on the West African route leave from Senegal, Morocco, Western Sahara and above all Mauritania. Tens of thousands of the illegal immigrants who have landed in the Canary Islands departed from Mauritania's coast.

In Nouadhibou, a local source told Muckraker that young migrant women are raped and held "like slaves," and that captors call their families to demand ransom. Asked whether criminals or police were responsible, he said both: "The police do that… because they are working with the criminals who smuggle people." He added that gun and drug traffickers travel among the migrants to get into Europe.

Muckraker also visited a migrant aid center in Nouadhibou run by OAMR (Organisation d'Appui et d'Assistance aux Migrants et Réfugiés), which works alongside the United Nations International Organization of Migration. A banner on the wall reads "Projet Julia Taft – Phase II": a capacity-building project offering training, outreach and assistance to refugees, asylum seekers and migrants in Nouadhibou, with funding listed as "Ambassade des Etats-Unis en Mauritanie" — the U.S. Embassy. Asked whether the United States pays for the center's bakery and computer lab too, staff answered yes.

The Julia Taft Refugee Fund is a State Department program run by the Bureau of Population, Refugees, and Migration. Created in 2000 and named for Julia Taft, who led that bureau under President Clinton, it lets U.S. embassies hand out small grants directly to local NGOs. The U.S. Embassy in Nouakchott's 2022 call for proposals offered up to $50,000 per project and listed migrants among eligible beneficiaries alongside refugees and returnees.

Arrival: The Canary Islands

Off the island of El Hierro, Muckraker filmed a boat packed with migrants, almost all of them military-aged men, being towed in by Spain's Maritime Rescue Service. One man was carried off on a stretcher, apparently lifeless.

Arrivals are taken to temporary camps. Residents described days with no work ("only eat and sleep") and men who leave to drink and try to come back with knives. A migrant from Senegal described a darker practice on the crossing itself: passengers accused of witchcraft are tied up and thrown into the sea.

The UN Insider: "Migration Is a Game"

On the Canary Islands, Muckraker met Sheikh M. Kromah, who was then working for the UN's International Organization for Migration (IOM) and has more than a decade in the migrant aid industry. Kromah has been photographed alongside Spain's Minister of Inclusion, Social Security and Migration, Elma Saiz, and local officials on El Hierro.

"The entire migration is a game," Kromah told Muckraker. "Everyone wants to have their share." He said smuggling networks collect between €50,000 and €60,000 per boat.

Asked why Spain doesn't stop the arrivals, he said the government doesn't want to. Every year, he said, Spain receives a huge amount of money from the European Union to manage migration, and if the boats stopped, so would the money. The strategy, in his words, is to "minimize it, but not stop it completely, so that they keep getting the money."

Kromah went further, claiming some of the money changes hands in cash, carried in suitcases into negotiating rooms. He said even the special police deployed to the islands, paid about three times a regular officer's salary, "want the boats to come every day."

"Everybody just wants to make money off everybody here," he said. "So if you look at it, it's a game."

Flown to the Mainland

Then comes the transfer. At Gran Canaria airport, Muckraker found a few hundred African men waiting to be flown to Madrid. This process happens multiple times per week and is managed by ACCEM.

ACCEM: The NGO Running Spain's Migrant Camps

One of the primary organizations responsible for moving illegal immigrants from the Canary Islands to mainland Spain, and housing them in camps once they arrive, is ACCEM.

ACCEM's full name is the Asociación Comisión Católica Española de Migración, the Spanish Catholic Commission for Migration. According to its own 2024 annual report, as reported by Spanish outlet Infovaticana, ACCEM took in about €225 million in 2024, 88% of it from Spain's central government. It employed 3,839 people and managed 9,812 reception places that year.

ACCEM makes no secret of its goals. In 2023, its president, Pilar Samanes Ara, cosigned a letter demanding more "safe and legal routes" for migrants into the European Union and Spain. The letter tied that demand directly to the UN's 2030 Agenda, describing migration as "a transformative force for growth and development."

Outside an ACCEM camp, Muckraker met a man from Senegal who had lived there for almost a year without a job. He said residents receive about €75 a month from ACCEM, plus bus or metro tickets. Even people who leave the camp without documents, he said, still get the money and a ticket. He knew of a friend who left for another Spanish city and kept being paid.

The UN's Blueprint

What Kromah described is consistent with the framework the UN itself has published. In September 2015, the UN General Assembly adopted the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, built around 17 Sustainable Development Goals.

In a related paper titled "Migration and the 2030 Agenda," the IOM states that the agenda recognizes migration as "a core development consideration," the first time migration has been integrated explicitly into the global development agenda. The paper calls migrant women, men and children "agents of development" and says migration can be linked to every goal in the 2030 Agenda. Its conclusion: efforts should not focus on stopping migration. Facilitating it, not restricting it, is the priority.

It is the same framework ACCEM's president invoked when demanding new routes into Europe. The UN sets the agenda, NGOs like ACCEM carry it out, and European taxpayers fund it.

A Painted Trail to France

In Irun, the last Spanish town before France, migrants arrive at the bus station on a daily basis. From the bus station, a trail of painted footsteps leads to the Red Cross and on to the town hall, where an activist group called Irungo Harrera Sarea meets migrants every day. Members of the activist group told Muckraker the group has helped some 40,000 migrants to cross the Spanish border into France.

The man who painted the footsteps told Muckraker the trail exists so migrants can cross the border without being caught by police, and that he plans to paint more "because they get lost." The activists confirmed they tell migrants which buses to take to avoid getting caught. A billboard by the train station maps out the entire route.

The trail leads to Pausa, a shelter in Bayonne, France, that has received millions of euros in public funds. Its director told Muckraker the center is managed by the city of Bayonne's administration and keeps "no photos, no names." Migrants stay a few days, he said, then take the bus and "go all over Europe," with or without documents.

Attacked in Paris

At the entrance to the Eiffel Tower, Muckraker found the plaza crowded with migrant street vendors. When the crew began filming, the vendors surrounded them. Muckraker co-founder Josh Rubin (@joshbrubin) was attacked and left bleeding heavily from the head, for pointing a camera.

A few miles away, Muckraker visited ARDHIS, an NGO that helps migrants seek asylum as LGBT refugees. A migrant who knows the community said many of those making the claim are not gay: "They say that they just want to get on… the help."

Calais and the Channel

For those headed to Britain, the last stop in France is Calais, where makeshift camps serve as staging grounds for Channel crossings. A local private security guard described migrants stealing from stores and killing a farmer's goat to eat. Human traffickers embed themselves in these camps, which have been the scene of deadly shootings in recent years.

Posing as aid workers and filming with hidden cameras, Muckraker got inside one camp set up in an abandoned warehouse. Men there said they came from Sudan, Morocco and Egypt. The crew counted roughly 100 tents packed under one roof, a prayer area lined with rugs and stacked Korans, and masked men watching the visitors. Once the camera was noticed, the mood turned. "I don't accept that you take photos here," one man said. A crowd closed in and pushed the crew out.

International trafficking networks run the crossings themselves. Many of the traffickers are illegal migrants themselves, often from Iraq, Albania and Kurdish regions. On the evening before a boat leaves, hundreds of migrants move out of the camps to pre-arranged meeting points along the coast. Muckraker spent weeks in Calais watching these movements and gathering intelligence.

Getting to a launch was the hard part. An Afghan migrant who planned to make the crossing himself told the crew that smugglers are suspicious of anyone who speaks English or French, assuming they are spies or police, and warned they could be beaten, injured or even killed. Late one night, he sent the crew the location where a boat would leave from, followed by a warning to be careful because the smugglers were armed.

The crew drove to the coast and waited. In the dark, they watched a dinghy head out to open water while groups of men they believed could be smugglers moved along the shore. The boat's plan was to circle back and pick up its passengers from the beach.

At about 5 a.m., more than 50 people ran out of the dunes toward the water, including a man carrying a small child. For more than 15 minutes, not a single police officer was on the beach. By the time police arrived, the boat was loading, and they soon gave up and walked back up the beach and the boat they attempted to stop successfully departed for and later arrived at the U.K.

The United Kingdom

In England, asylum seekers living in a government-funded hotel told Muckraker that housing and food are free, that they receive about £300 a month, and that university is free for them as well. One said he had been living in the hotel for three years.

title: Global Gas Crunch Makes Europe's Remaining Coal Plants Profitable
desc:
Global Gas Crunch Makes Europe's Remaining Coal Plants Profitable

By Michael Kern of OilPrice.com

The global LNG supply crunch has made Europe’s last-standing coal-fired power plants profitable this year as gas supply costs soar while the need for conventional generation to stabilize grids remains.

In Germany and Poland, which host most of the remaining operational or back-up-ready coal power capacity in Europe, coal-fired generation is profitable again as winter approaches, LNG supply is barely moving out of the Strait of Hormuz, and gas prices are at their highest level since the 2022-2023 crisis.

European countries, including Germany, have closed coal capacities in recent years due to climate targets. But the remaining coal-fired power plants have now become indispensable in stabilizing the grids as gas-fired generation slumps amid demand destruction and gas conservation.

One measure of profitability for generating electricity from lignite in Germany has jumped to as much as $72 (64 euros) per megawatt-hour (MWh) this month, compared to zero at this time last year, per estimates by Energy Aspects cited by Bloomberg.

“The spreads are expected to stay high through March,” Energy Aspects analyst Sabrina Kernbichler said.

Coal demand in Europe remains in a structural decline, but the drop is set to slow this year, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said in its Coal Mid-Year Update 2026 last month.

Total annual coal demand in Europe is now expected to reach 276 million tons in 2026, down from 292 million tons last year, but higher than previously expected, according to the agency.

“Higher gas prices have reduced the expected decline in countries, such as Germany and Poland, where gas generation and spare coal capacity remains available,” the IEA noted.

Weather-related events, such as cold spells going into the winter, could also temporarily increase coal use in Europe more than what was expected before the war in Iran, which sent shockwaves through the oil and gas markets globally, the Paris-based agency said.

title: Under Pressure From Trump, EU Introduces Corporate Levy Instead Of Digital Tax
desc:
Under Pressure From Trump, EU Introduces Corporate Levy Instead Of Digital Tax

Submitted by Thomas Kolbe

In the end, are we working only for the state? What was once dismissed as a light-hearted exaggeration is becoming reality step by step. In the midst of the worst economic crisis since the end of World War II, Germany has developed a fever for taxation. Berlin is raising levies unreasonably, from the sugar tax to tobacco and alcohol taxes, from higher top income-tax rates and the super-rich tax to the highly probable increase in inheritance tax – increasingly, the substance of the middle class is also coming into the sights of Berlin’s central planners.

Berlin has launched a species-threatening hunt for the taxpayer.

It is truly an absurd idea, if not knowingly destructive policy, to keep expanding the state apparatus at the expense of the private sector in order to overcome a crisis that this very state apparatus has brought about with its ideology, its degrowth policies and its boundless belief in what can be engineered.

But as if this tax policy were not already fatal enough, Brussels too is demanding an increasing share of the shrinking economic pie. The Commission is feeling the growing pressure to finance itself. From 2028 onward, the refinancing of the €800 billion NextGenerationEU Eurobond will come due. Ursula von der Leyen also wants to lock in her two-trillion-euro budget as quickly and quietly as possible. Every new source of tax revenue therefore comes in handy.

The state paradox is this: The more capital or credit politicians have at their disposal, the faster new demands, new follow-up costs and economic ruins emerge – the state is the great maw into which citizens can pour tax money at will – in the end, it always cries out for more and more.

So far, the EU Commission has primarily collected funds from EU customs revenues. There are also extraction vehicles such as the CO₂ emissions trading system and its own plastic tax.

To expand its tax base, Brussels originally planned to introduce a digital levy. Large digital companies, platforms such as Google, Amazon and X, were to be bled for their contribution to the common good, as the argument always goes. The Brussels Commission officially abandoned this plan this week – the pressure from Washington, namely from the US president himself, apparently proved too great to maintain these plans.

Instead, a special levy on large corporations operating economically in the EU is now planned. It would be an annual flat-rate charge for companies with net revenues of more than €100 million. Depending on the revenue class, the contribution would range from €100,000 to €750,000 per year. That sounds like a trifle, payable out of the petty cash of many large corporations. But every little bit adds up. And so Brussels repeatedly succeeds in creating the impression that the gigantic fiscal raid burdens only a few wealthy people, spares the middle class and ultimately remains within limits.

Beyond the fiscal dimension, the planned digital tax naturally also had a trade-policy function. It was conceived as a weapon, directed against the Chinese and American digital corporations that have left the Europeans hopelessly behind technologically. The logic was: If you cannot compete, at least collect plenty of taxes from them.

We know this all too well from Brussels.

With the Digital Services Act and Digital Markets Act, the Brussels Commission developed mechanisms to derive regular heavy fines from the supposed grey zone in which the digital corporations operate – through alleged violations of copyright rules or through a lack of consumer and data protection – an eternal source of irritation and continuing provocations that by no means contribute to pacifying the American-European relationship.

With the planned digital levy, this extraction policy was supposed to be cast into a foundation. A secure financial stream for Brussels was planned, but the White House ultimately eliminated it with a firm hand.

That it is now European companies, of all companies, those economically engaged in the EU, that will step into the breach to fill this already budgeted revenue is typical of this EU: Bureaucracy requires higher tax burdens. A power structure has become entrenched that now increasingly develops its own sources of taxation like an autonomous state.

What we are actually witnessing is a bidding war over the fight for the slowly shrinking tax pie at every level of government.

It must be said plainly: The Brussels power apparatus, having solidified into an extraction mechanism, appears impossible to reform. New political forces will be needed to rebuild this structure so that it serves the interests of European citizens. A common protection of the EU’s external borders and the revival of the single market would be major projects of absolute priority. The taxpayer-funded system of patronage must come to an end.

Economic constructs such as the Green Deal and the absurd subsidy sectors created from it, from the hydrogen economy to the storage of CO₂ in the seabed, consume ever larger sums in subsidies and government support year after year. Uncontrollably high government debt, deepening crowding-out of the private sector in the capital and labour markets, as well as the increasing drain of resources to finance this bankrupt economy, are the harvest reaped by a society that places its fate in the hands of these ideologues.

The debt and tax spirals inevitably turn in sync. They are spinning faster and make it clear that higher government spending and higher tax payments will solve none of the numerous problems created by the modern party state.

European bureaucratism has married German statism. Faith in free enterprise, in the free market economy as an institutional model for prosperity, democracy and individual sovereignty, has been lost in the ever deeper corridors of the administrative machinery.

The wait for EU citizens to recognise the historically well-documented superiority of civil society over every form of statist interpretation has begun – a tough, frustrating undertaking that nevertheless brings us closer, with time, to the inevitable debt crisis. And crisis, as we know, means a turning point.

In the small town of Harsefeld in Lower Saxony, a youth gang active for at least six months committed beatings, threats, extortion, and drug trafficking, uploading videos of the assaults.

Two known leaders had approximately 15 reported crimes each. Citizens formed a vigilante patrol group to protect children after police response was criticized as inadequate. A police spokesperson said: "Yes, of course, we find that quite creepy. A vigilante group doesn't help anyone."

The filmed attack in Frankfurt (Oder) is not an outlier. It is one more instance in which German students have been surrounded, beaten, and filmed by groups that include large numbers of foreign nationals and those with migration backgrounds.

Officials issue statements of outrage and schedule further talks while the underlying numbers on school violence and the composition of the suspects remain consistent across multiple reports. Native German children continue to encounter these conditions on the way to and from school.

title: Le Pen And AfD Join Forces: Heavy Headwinds For Von Der Leyen's EU Mega-Budget
desc:
Le Pen And AfD Join Forces: Heavy Headwinds For Von Der Leyen's EU Mega-Budget

Submitted by Thomas Kolbe

A breather in the European bond market.

After yields on ten-year French government bonds brushed against the 5-percent mark in late trading on Friday, the situation calmed again at the start of the week. Two politically significant developments, one from Germany and the other from France, apparently acted like circuit breakers as they are known in the markets.

On Monday, an AfD strategy paper was circulating. In this pamphlet, the party’s European policy experts had apparently agreed on a strategic shift in their approach to the EU and monetary policy. There was no longer any talk of leaving the euro system or even of a Dexit, Germany’s departure from the European Union.

Quite the opposite: The EU is to be transformed into a federation of sovereign nations, with a focus on the internal market, effective protection of the external borders, and coordination among member states on security matters. In general, the goal should be to return political powers to the nation-states — all sensible measures to consolidate the EU’s completely out-of-control expansionism.

As for the shaky euro currency, the authors of the paper argue that it should rest on a solid foundation of individual states taking responsibility for themselves and assuming their own liabilities. Whether this can put an end to the tiresome problem of shifting fiscal responsibility onto German taxpayers remains to be seen.

Important for opponents of fiat money: According to the AfD, the European Central Bank should have its operational scope significantly restricted. Specifically, the paper calls for an end to “indirect ECB financing of governments,” the settlement of Target balances, and an insolvency regime for member states. A ban on financing government debt with the central bank’s money printer would be a revolution in monetary policy. It would be the end of ideological experiments. Politics would have to abandon vehicles such as the Green Deal, since its economic stillbirths can only be kept alive with the help of manipulated borrowing costs. In light of the latest bond turmoil, any means would be justified to leave this destructive path behind.

All of this points in the right direction, but avoids a break with existing power structures. After all, nothing frightens the markets more than uncertainty. A clear horizon is what they are looking for, which is why the news from Germany likely contributed to a collective sigh of relief in the bond market.

France’s opposition leader Marine Le Pen of the Rassemblement National sounded similarly tame. On Tuesday morning, Le Pen presented her plans to consolidate France’s ailing public finances.

A partial return to the Maastricht criteria, with annual new borrowing below three percent of GDP, is what she is seeking, Le Pen said. That, however, would require a revival of economic activity, in an economy that, much like Germany’s, is bloodless and starved of innovation under Brussels’ climate diktat. The country is heading toward sovereign bankruptcy, the politician said, and by 2032, hard spending cuts are supposed to generate savings of €140 billion.

After just 15 months in office, Le Pen plans to achieve a balanced primary budget, meaning a surplus before interest payments. As in Germany, Le Pen plans to enshrine a debt brake, her “golden rule,” in the constitution by referendum — and we have known since Chancellor Friedrich Merz single-handedly executed the debt brake with an already-defeated Bundestag and the special fund exactly what such political promises are worth.

Le Pen also had a very special message for Ursula von der Leyen. France’s net contributions to the European Commission should immediately be cut back to the level of the early 2000s, to five billion euros. A reduction of around 64 percent.

If Le Pen wins the election, she could put herself at the head of a consolidation movement that clips Brussels’ expansionist wings. Von der Leyen is planning a two-trillion-euro mega-budget for the period from 2028 to 2034 - a hyperbolic expansion of 60 percent, which would send Germany’s contribution to the debt club soaring from around €27 billion today to €40–45 billion a year. Even the otherwise debt-friendly Friedrich Merz is trying to rein in this expansionist drive somewhat. Media theater, without a doubt, but the chancellor senses that there is no longer any backing for this policy.

Ultimately, the question is whether Europe will increasingly pool its debt in eurobonds, into a common pool consolidated under the roof of the European Commission and systematically monetized by the European Central Bank. A shell game: shifting the costs of debt-making onto EU taxpayers, who ultimately become the pack animals of centralism, central planning and state-run economics — all systems that consume more billions year after year.

Perhaps the bond market received reassuring signals from the European right. If it is able to put the brakes on this fiscal crash course, a consolidated EU focused on its core responsibilities could take shape. The AfD paper offers important indications of a realistic path toward that goal.

For more than three decades, Michael Gove has been a leading figure in British Conservatism. As a journalist, government minister and now editor of the Tory bible, the Spectator, he has helped shape the right even as it has moved further rightwards. In the latest episode of Radical Thinking, Gove joins Aditya Chakrabortty to discuss the future of the right, his record on Brexit and austerity, and the Spectator’s position on Islam

Watch the full episode with Michael Gove here.

Aditya’s suggested reading:

To read the fruits of Michael Gove’s dalliance with the Marxism Today gang, look up his essay in a 1998 collection called The Moderniser’s Dilemma: Radical Politics in the Age of Blair

For slalom ride through Michael Gove’s years in power, read The Demented Dalek by the historian Richard J Evans in the London Review of Books

To learn more on what’s become of the British right, there’s a column by me for the Guardian

Just why the most successful political party is now failing is analysed in-depth by Phil Burton-Cartledge in his book The Party’s Over: The Rise and Fall of the Conservatives from Thatcher to Sunak

Phil also writes a very good blog on British politics, which keeps a close eye on how each party is trying to marshall a coalition of voters. Here he is on Kemi Badenoch

Finally, on the Spectator read Nesrine Malik’s recent column in The Guardian

title: Everything Is Russia's Fault (Even Global Warming!)
desc:
Everything Is Russia's Fault (Even Global Warming!)

Authored by J.B. Shurk via American Thinker,

In the old days (which, in the age of social media, were only ten years or so ago), every problem in the world was blamed on "global warming."

Hot summers? Global warming. Cold winters? That was global warming, too. Christian churches mysteriously burning to the ground? Ooh...obviously global warming. Endless hordes of foreigners breaking into the country? Global warming disproportionately affects third-world s-holes and causes military-aged men to run North, dontcha know. The spread of COVID? Oh, that definitely didn't come from a Chinese bio-lab receiving money from the esteemed pharmaceutical salesman Dr. Fauci; that virus was totally the fault of global warming!

According to the "experts," global warming caused every policy failure, government screwup, international brouhaha, and economic downturn of the last few decades (at least when card-carrying globalists, "progressives," new-world-order types, or other assorted leftists were in power). "Science" said so. And if you didn't believe the "experts," well, then, you were just an ignorant science-denier!

Since 2016, a new scapegoat - I mean, fact-based and expertly diagnosed cause - for all the world's problems has been hogging global warming's spotlight: Russia, Russia, Russia.

Read something that you don't like? That's gotta be Russian disinformation. The "wrong" candidate wins an election? Never would have happened without Russian social media bots! Energy prices are too low? That's because of cheap Russian oil and gas. Energy prices are too high? That's because Russia - and definitely not Ukraine! - blew up its own Nord Stream pipelines delivering inexpensive energy to Europe. Military-aged Muslims are raping and stabbing Europeans across the continent? Ooh, trick question - that's a global-warming-Russia tag-team! Everybody with a PhD in political science knows that Europe's inability to secure its own borders is totally Vladimir Putin's fault!

Didn't the Norwegian Nobel Committee award the Peace Prize to climate doomsayer Al Gore (who predicted that we'd all be under water by now) and the United Nations' Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change for figuring out that all of the problems in the world can be traced to hydrocarbons and free markets? Surely the prizes in chemistry, physics, medicine, and literature will eventually go to well-credentialed "experts" who determine that Russia is actually to blame for everything.

This Nobel Prize-worthy epiphany has been rattling in my head because I noticed that the United Kingdom's recently installed prime minister, Andy Burnham, is considering whether to reverse Brexit and rejoin the European Union since - you guessed it! - Russia somehow manipulated the 2016 referendum in favor of decoupling! Burnham - who won a small special election to gain his seat in Parliament only last summer and lacks anything remotely approaching a general mandate from the whole kingdom - says Russia's Brexit "interference" was "clear." His pronouncement seems to contradict multiple parliamentary investigations - including those from the anti-Brexit Electoral Commission - which have all concluded that there was "no evidence of successful interference in the EU Referendum."

Other prominent members of Burnham's Labour Party are giddy about the prospect of rejoining the E.U., but all insist that no new referendum should be held for voters to decide the matter. title: Chinese Researchers Unveil Plans For Tank That Can Remain Submerged For Two Hours
desc:
Chinese Researchers Unveil Plans For Tank That Can Remain Submerged For Two Hours

China is working on a military vehicle concept that could allow a tank to remain underwater for up to two hours, potentially giving its armed forces a new way to approach enemy coastlines during amphibious operations, according to the South China Morning Post.

The proposed system would allow an armored vehicle to travel at depths of up to 164 feet before emerging from the water and continuing its mission on land. The idea is to give military forces greater flexibility during coastal assaults while reducing their reliance on traditional landing equipment.

SCMP writes that the project, developed by researchers at the Inner Mongolia First Machinery Group and Beijing Institute of Technology, is part of a larger effort to create military vehicles capable of rapidly adapting to different battlefield conditions.

Rather than designing separate vehicles for every environment, researchers are experimenting with interchangeable modules that could allow a single platform to perform multiple roles. The proposed vehicles would also incorporate drones to help clear obstacles and potentially accelerate amphibious landings.

On land, the hybrid-powered platform is envisioned as having a range of roughly 373 miles and reaching speeds of more than 43 mph. Researchers are also targeting a nine-second response time between identifying a threat and launching an attack.

Initial testing has demonstrated promising results for the vehicle's modular components, but the underwater capabilities have not yet been proven. The researchers have not disclosed how fast the vehicle could travel underwater or how far it could move while submerged.

The concept is part of China's longer-term military technology planning for the period between 2030 and 2050, as researchers explore how armored vehicles might operate across multiple combat environments.

title: New Dementia Cases Projected To More Than Double Globally By 2050
desc:
New Dementia Cases Projected To More Than Double Globally By 2050

Authored by Naveen Athrappully via The Epoch Times,

The number of new annual dementia cases worldwide is estimated to increase more than twofold by 2050 from 2023 levels, according to a recently published peer-reviewed study.

Published in the JAMA Neurology journal on Oct. 12, the study analyzed data from more than 38,000 individuals across 18 nations and territories.

Based on the calculated incidence rate of dementia, the researchers estimated that in 2050, there would be 24.7 million new cases worldwide, up by more than 116 percent from 11.4 million new cases in 2023.

Gender-wise, incidence rates were found to be higher among women than men.

Middle-income and lower-income nations had higher rates than richer countries.

In an Oct. 13 statement, the University of New South Wales Sydney, whose researchers led the study, said that dementia already affects more than 57 million people globally.

Prof. Henry Brodaty, co-author of the study, said in a statement that the findings reinforce the urgent need to invest in dementia prevention measures.

"Twenty-four million new cases of dementia every year would place enormous pressure on individuals, families, health systems and economies around the world," Brodaty said.

"Population ageing means we cannot simply wait for people to develop dementia and then respond," Brodaty said.

"We need to act across the spectrum - from reducing modifiable risk factors and identifying people at risk earlier, through to improving diagnosis, treatment and care."

Understanding incidence rate was critical as it helps estimate future demand for diagnoses and clinical care, while contributing to preparing the requisite preventive measures, the statement said.

Prof. Perminder Sachdev, senior author of the study, said that higher incidence rates in low- and middle-income nations were "particularly concerning because these regions are experiencing rapid population ageing while often having the fewest resources for prevention, diagnosis and care."

Dementia is used to describe a decline in mental ability that interferes with daily life, with the most common type being Alzheimer's.

"The sooner you can diagnose dementia, the sooner you can begin to treat it to slow its progression," the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said in an August 2024 report.

Dementia affects more than 6 million Americans and is the reason for more than 100,000 deaths annually, according to a February 2025 post by the National Institutes of Health (NIH).

Researchers estimate that 42 percent of Americans above the age of 55 could eventually end up developing dementia, and U.S. population aging is expected to double the annual new dementia case numbers by 2060, NIH said.

Some of the risk factors for dementia include lack of physical activity, alcohol or tobacco use, high blood pressure, uncontrolled diabetes, and loss of hearing, according to the CDC.

The agency recommended engaging in physical activity regularly to help prevent, delay, or manage chronic medical conditions such as dementia.

It asked people to avoid or restrict smoking and alcohol consumption.

"High blood pressure can damage blood vessels and limit blood flow to the brain, which does damage to the brain. It also increases the risk of having a stroke, which can also damage the brain," CDC said.

"Maintaining a healthy weight and taking your prescribed blood pressure medications can help."

Meanwhile, researchers are investigating new methods for identifying dementia risk earlier. A study published in the JAMA Network Open journal in March found that a blood test could help in predicting dementia among women up to 25 years before symptom onset.

The study analyzed blood samples of females for plasma p-tau217, a type of protein that indicates early brain changes associated with Alzheimer's.

"We observed a 3-fold higher hazard of all-cause dementia with higher baseline p-tau217 levels," the study said.

The association of p-tau217 with mild cognitive impairment or dementia was "greater among women older than 70 years."

title: Qatar's Government Revenue Plunges 42% In First Half As Iran War Knocks Out Gas Exports
desc:
Qatar's Government Revenue Plunges 42% In First Half As Iran War Knocks Out Gas Exports

Qatar's government revenue fell 42% in the first half of 2026, Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani told the Shura Council on Tuesday, October 13. The figure puts an official number on the damage that the Iran war and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz have inflicted on what was previously the world's second-largest liquefied natural gas (LNG) exporter. Public spending also fell 14% over the same six months, the emir added as he opened the council's annual session in Doha.

"It is only natural that the crisis would have a negative impact on public finances," the emir said, according to TRT World. Still, he emphasized that the government will not cut essential services or alter its development goals. He credited the financial cushion Qatar built before the war–larger reserves, lower public debt, and conservative oil-price assumptions–and pointed to roughly QR221 billion ($60.7 billion) in projects and investments planned over the next five years.

Quarterly figures show just how fast the budget shortfall grew. According to Finance Ministry data carried by the state news agency QNA, the second-quarter deficit hit QR21.2 billion (on QR25.6 billion in revenue against QR46.8 billion in spending)–roughly double the first quarter's QR10.3 billion gap. That brings the first-half deficit to about QR31.5 billion, already 1.4 times the QR21.8 billion shortfall projected for all of 2026.

Second-quarter revenue plunged 57% compared to a year earlier, when the deficit was just QR800 million, AGBI reported. Drawn up in December, the 2026 budget had assumed oil at $55 a barrel, total revenue of QR199 billion, and spending of QR220.8 billion.

The financial hit stems directly from damaged energy infrastructure. In early March, an Iranian drone strike forced the massive Ras Laffan gas complex to shut down, prompting state-owned QatarEnergy to halt LNG production and suspend its contract obligations to buyers–a legal move known as force majeure, as we reported at the time. As we noted in June, the Washington Post reported that the strikes also ended secret Qatari efforts to keep the complex off Iran's target list.

Subsequent Iranian missile strikes on Ras Laffan knocked out two of Qatar's 14 gas-processing units–wiping out 12.8 million tons of annual output, or 17% of its export capacity–along with one of its two gas-to-liquids plants. QatarEnergy warned at the time that the units would take three to five years to repair, costing an estimated $20 billion a year in lost revenue, and suspended long-term supply deals with buyers including Italy's Edison and South Korea's KOGAS, Reuters reported. "For production to restart, first we need hostilities to cease," QatarEnergy chief Saad al-Kaabi said.

An October 15 Reuters investigation revealed the root of the delay: the strikes destroyed two "cold boxes," the specialized core equipment used to super-chill natural gas into a liquid at Ras Laffan. Across the region, Reuters tallied at least 135 missile and drone attacks hitting 84 or more infrastructure sites since the war began.

There are minor signs of recovery in other areas of processing. On October 8, Shell announced it had partially restarted the Pearl gas-to-liquids plant, allowing it to slowly rebuild inventory, though actual shipments still depend on regional security. Repairs to the plant's damaged second processing unit are expected to wrap up in early 2027.

Seven months into the conflict, however, very little gas is leaving the country. Qatar exported 1.6 million tons of LNG in September–its highest monthly total since the war began, but still less than a quarter of its pre-war average, with about a third of that staying inside the Gulf for Kuwait. Data firm Kpler projected on October 12 that October shipments would drop to just 0.6 million tons, according to Reuters.

The supply crunch is rippling through Europe. Edison said on September 28 that QatarEnergy had extended its supply suspension to early December, bringing the Italian utility's total disrupted shipments to 35 cargoes since April. The uncertainty prompted French energy giant EDF to pause plans to sell a stake in Edison, CEO Nicola Monti told Reuters on October 14. Monti said he hoped deliveries would resume in early 2027, but admitted there is "no visibility at this stage."

Last week, at least 12 empty QatarEnergy tankers–capable of holding about 1.1 million tons of gas, or 2% of the world's LNG shipping fleet–were massing off the coast in an apparent bid to load up and make a run through the Strait of Hormuz. In his speech, the emir condemned the strikes as an Iranian attack on Qatari sovereignty, while Tehran maintains it was only targeting US interests, Euronews noted.

To plug its budget gap, Doha has returned to the bond market. In September, Qatar sold $3 billion in five- and 10-year bonds–its first international public debt sale since November–drawing over $7.7 billion in buyer orders, Bloomberg reported. The same month, credit agency Fitch removed Qatar from its downgrade watch list, citing a lower risk of further severe damage to its gas plants.

Meanwhile, the broader economy is feeling the squeeze. National Planning Council figures released on September 30 via QNA showed Qatar's oil and gas sector shrank 50.7% year-over-year in the second quarter, while the rest of the economy grew 2.6%. The emir noted that non-energy industries now account for roughly 80% of overall economic output. Still, the IMF now expects Qatar's economy to shrink 15.6% this year–nearly double the 8.6% drop it projected in April–before rebounding 18.8% in 2027 if the Strait of Hormuz reopens. The fund released the downgraded forecasts on the same day as the emir's speech.

Despite the disruption, the emir said work on the North Field expansion–a massive project aimed at boosting Qatar's LNG capacity to 142 million tons a year by 2030–is still moving ahead on schedule. Qatar Chamber chairman Sheikh Khalifa bin Jassim Al Thani praised the government's handling of the crisis, telling The Peninsula that protecting essential services despite plunging revenues proves the state's commitment to stability.

title: US Offers Another 17 Million SPR Barrels As Fuel Crisis Deepens
desc:
US Offers Another 17 Million SPR Barrels As Fuel Crisis Deepens

By Julianne Geiger of OilPrice.com,

The United States is putting another 17 million barrels of crude from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve on offer, one day after the IEA accelerated emergency stock releases as governments scramble to get more oil and fuel into a tight market.

The Department of Energy issued a request for proposals Friday for an exchange of up to 17 million barrels, part of the 172 million barrels Washington committed to make available under the IEA’s 400-million-barrel emergency action announced in March.

The SPR currently holds about 283 million barrels. If companies take the full 17 million barrels before any repayments arrive, inventories would fall to roughly 266 million barrels—squarely inside the 250-million-to-300-million-barrel range generally considered the reserve’s operational minimum zone.

There is one rather large catch: somebody has to want the oil.

DOE offered the final portion of its March commitment in June, requiring companies to return the borrowed crude later with premiums of as much as 24%. Companies agreed to take only about 500,000 barrels.

The government is trying again. The API estimated that U.S. crude stocks fell 11.12 million barrels last week, following a 2.09-million-barrel decline the previous week. Commercial inventories have lost more than 51 million barrels over the last 26 weeks.

Friday’s solicitation follows another escalation in the emergency-stock campaign. The IEA said Thursday that members would accelerate the roughly 100 million barrels still outstanding from March, including more than 20 million barrels of diesel as soon as possible.

Washington is now putting 17 million more barrels on the table, with the SPR sitting at 283 million barrels in a market that already showed once this summer that borrowing government crude on expensive repayment terms is not necessarily a deal refiners want.
